prediction.action: First compare channel-presence timelines with digitizer-board boundaries and the anomaly onset by subrun. Check MilliDAQ/DAQ logs for restarts, readout errors, synchronization loss, queue saturation, or high CPU usage, and compare digitizer event rates against trigger-board rates. If omissions align with one digitizer, inspect its synchronization and lock state and conditionally restart that digitizer/DAQ PC using the approved procedure; if omissions are system-wide and coincide with a DAQ restart or CPU saturation, conditionally restart MilliDAQ or address the host load instead. Do not pursue PMT/HV repairs unless HV logs or channel-local pulse/LVDS behavior independently supports them.

The count drop near subrun 40 occurs without a comparable rate anomaly and may reflect exposure length rather than detector behavior. INFERRED: healthy trigger/LVDS summaries argue against a trigger-board or localized LVDS failure and make an intermittent downstream DAQ/digitizer readout problem more plausible. Runs 1500, 1604, 1605, and 1620 provide partial analogies involving pulse-count anomalies with DAQ restart, high CPU, or digitizer lockup, but there is no exact historical match. A PMT-base failure is less supported because the pattern is widespread and no abnormal LVDS pin is reported. UNKNOWN: digitizer rates, board grouping of missing channels, synchronization/lock status, CPU and queue telemetry, restart logs, within-run configuration changes, and HV status are required to distinguish DAQ restart, host overload, digitizer lockup, or data-processing artifacts.
